trigger: A hospital reports IX-3 settings or drug library limits changed without a clinician; any allegation the device failed to meet specifications
deadline: Open at receipt; investigate and record required details
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Medical Devices is the manufacturer
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)

trigger: Information reasonably suggests the device may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or malfunctioned in a way likely to cause one if it recurred
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected in this scenario (unauthorized dose limit change; one over-infusion event under investigation)
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)

trigger: An MDR reportable event necessitates remedial action to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the public health, or FDA asks in writing
deadline: No later than 5 work days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Decision point: likely if the field campaign is judged remedial action to prevent substantial harm
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)
clock_starts: Day the company becomes aware of the need for remedial action

trigger: New information that was not known when the initial MDR was submitted
deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - forensic findings will add information
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)

trigger: A correction or removal initiated to reduce a risk to health (unless already reported under Part 803 or exempt under 806.1(b))
deadline: Within 10 working days of initiating the correction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the field update campaign and customer advisory are a correction; see the enforcement-discretion row
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)

obligation: FDA enforcement discretion for uncontrolled cybersecurity risk (in place of an 806 report)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (Dec. 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Uncontrolled risk to essential performance
deadline: Customers told within 30 days of learning of the vulnerability, with compensating controls; fix distributed within 60 days; no known serious adverse events or deaths; active ISAO participation
applies_at_this_tier: Condition not met in this scenario if the over-infusion is confirmed as a serious injury; then report under 806.10
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (Chief Product Security Officer; VP Quality and Regulatory Affairs)
clock_starts: Date the company learned of the vulnerability or exploit

trigger: A correction or removal that is not required to be reported (for example, a routine cybersecurity update for a controlled risk)
deadline: Keep the record; retain 2 years beyond the expected life of the device
applies_at_this_tier: Only for controlled-risk updates

obligation: Customer advisory to hospitals using IX-3
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (Dec. 2016); customer contracts
trigger: Uncontrolled risk or confirmed exploitation
deadline: Interim phone calls to affected hospitals on Day 0-1; written advisory within 30 days of learning of the vulnerability (target Day 7 here)
notify: Clinical engineering, CISO, and pharmacy contacts at about 700 hospitals with IX-3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Medical Devices (customer support director with the CPSO)
clock_starts: Date the company learned of the vulnerability or exploit

obligation: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure and public advisory
citation: FD&C Act 524B(b)(1) plan commitments (for 524B devices); published CVD policy
trigger: Vulnerability affecting a marketed device
deadline: Per the CVD policy and the agreed disclosure date; optionally coordinated through CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - IX-3 is outside 524B but covered by the group CVD policy (POL-01 4.8)

obligation: User facility MDR (the hospitals' own duty)
trigger: A device may have caused or contributed to a patient death (to FDA and manufacturer) or serious injury (to manufacturer)
deadline: No more than 10 work days after the facility becomes aware
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's obligation. Expect reports from affected hospitals and feed them into the complaint file

trigger: Distribution receives a complaint alleging IX-3 deficiencies (for example from a customer it supplied)
deadline: Record at receipt; forward to Medical Devices the same day (division supplement)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Distribution is a distributor for IX-3 service and exchange units

obligation: Distribution hold and customer notice support
trigger: Medical Devices initiates a correction affecting stock Distribution holds or customers it supplied
deadline: Hold within 4 hours of the manufacturer's request (division supplement); customer lists within 24 hours
notify: Distribution centers; Distribution customers (with the manufacturer's advisory)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 1,140 refurbished IX-3 exchange units and spare boards in stock

trigger: Importer product line involved
deadline: Deaths and serious injuries to FDA and manufacturer, malfunctions to manufacturer, within 30 calendar days
applies_at_this_tier: No - IX-3 is not an imported product. Keep for incidents involving importer lines

obligation: Federal customers (VA and DoD facilities using IX-3)
citation: Contract communications; no FAR clause requires a product vulnerability report
trigger: IX-3 units at federal facilities
deadline: Same advisory and timing as other hospitals, sent through the contracting officer and facility biomedical contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - courtesy and contract relationship, not a legal notice duty (verify with the contract)
notifying_entity: Distribution (federal contracts compliance director) with Medical Devices

trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system (one that processes covered defense information)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery (rapidly report)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no covered defense information; recheck if any group system that holds CDI is affected

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only if identified (not part of this scenario)

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held in the DCC
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; BAA terms shorter (15 calendar days standard; 5 days for 64 health systems)
notify: Each affected hospital (covered entity), identifying each affected individual
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (IX-3 does not connect to the DCC). Decide at every product incident (POL-03 4.5)

trigger: Security incident affecting the DCC without a breach of PHI
deadline: Per BAA (5 business days in the standard BAA)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the DCC is involved

obligation: Hospital's own breach decision for pump logs
trigger: IX-3 pump event logs (under hospital control) contain patient identifiers and were accessed by the attacker
deadline: Hospitals' clocks run from their own discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's obligation; tell hospitals what data the pump stores so they can decide

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents held by the group (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if group-held personal information is involved (not in this scenario). Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents held by the group
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (up to 15 more days for good cause, individual notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if group-held personal information is involved
notifying_entity: Group entity that owns the data

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the threshold is met

trigger: A third-party agent maintaining information for a covered entity discovers a breach
deadline: Within 10 days of determination or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the DCC (acting for Florida hospitals) is breached

trigger: Incident affecting a client's confidential data held by Testing
deadline: Per NDA (most require prompt notice; terms being added to this matrix, POAM-004)
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario; Testing holds embargoed findings on the same component for another client and must not share them (barrier)

trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant; disclosure committee decides

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management and governance, including product security; lessons from the incident may inform it

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Confirmed criminal exploitation of a medical device
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0-2 target)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA (coordinated vulnerability disclosure for medical devices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended

citation: FDA postmarket guidance (Dec. 2016) enforcement-discretion condition; ISAO membership terms
trigger: Vulnerability or exploit affecting marketed devices
deadline: Share the customer communication and indicators with the ISAO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - active member

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary

trigger: Suspected security incident with possible loss
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
